## 2282d057d92e

**Reproduced teaching shortcut; audited target left unchanged.** The pinned
generator SHA-256 is
`b1b6d35f7203ccfef28be6bae247ad474e44e73a0b23fa87076fcc6ad0b3cf21`
and the executed canonical rule hash is `e97c9d96fbf7`.

All three canonical demonstrations use each color at most once. Therefore the
plausible rival “only the first row-major occurrence of each color casts
rightward” matches every canonical demonstration. The production sampler does
emit counterexamples, but it has no declared semantic rival or lesson contract
guaranteeing that every assembled lesson contains one.

Using seed `0`, sample index `0`, difficulty `medium`, the first generated input
reuses color `6` on three separate rows. The public `apply` command reports that
input as valid in the documented generator domain and paints all three rays; the
rival paints only the first. The exact input, actual Racket output, rival output,
canonical-fit checks, hashes, and commands are in
`checks/audit/2282d057d92e/counterexample.json`. Supporting files are
`checks/audit/2282d057d92e/input.json`,
`checks/audit/2282d057d92e/racket.json`, and
`checks/audit/2282d057d92e/reproduce.py`.

This is a lesson-coverage finding, not evidence that generated labels are wrong.
A repair should declare the rival and guarantee a repeated-color witness in each
supported lesson/query policy.
